The plaintiff has filed this suit seeking the following reliefs:
(a) Declaration that the sale deed dated 21.06.1990 executed by defendant No.3 in favour of defendant No.4 and sale deed dated 29.08.2003 executed by defendant No.4 in favour of defendant No.5 are not binding on the plaintiff in respect of suit schedule-B property.

(b) Permanent injunction restraining defendant Nos.3 to 5, their agents or anyone claiming under them, from interfering with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule-A property.
(c) Mandatory injunction directing defendant Nos.3 to 5 to demolish the structure constructed on suit schedule-B property.
(d) Directing defendant No.6 to enter encumbrances in the official records regarding the suit property and such other favourable reliefs.

2. The brief averments of the plaint are as follows: -
The suit pertains to the property bearing Survey No.66/5, measuring 26 guntas,
situated at Dommalur Village, Kasaba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk i.e., suit schedule-A property, with a portion thereof i.e., suit schedule-B property being the subject of the disputed sale deeds and construction by defendant No.5.

The plaintiff,
widow of Late Ramaiah, claims that her father-in- law - Late Siddappa, was the absolute owner of land in Survey No.66/5 (26 guntas) in Dommalur Village, Kasaba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, acquired through the registered sale deed dated 1967-68.
The revenue records were mutated in the name of Siddappa.

2(a). After the death of Siddappa on 26.01.2005 and death of Ramaiah on 05.03.2003, the plaintiff inherited the property through an oral partition among family members, with her children relinquishing their rights in her favour.
The plaintiff asserts lawful possession, supported by BBMP khatha certificates (PID No.72-13-66/5), tax payment receipts and revenue entries.

2(b). In 1981, the State of Karnataka - defendant No.1 issued a Notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act bearing No.LAQ (1) SR 12/1981-82, dated 28.12.1981 to acquire 82 acres 19 guntas, including Survey No.66/5, for the benefit of Amarajyothi House Building Co-operative Society - defendant No.3.
A Final Notification under Section 6(1) was issued on 14.10.1982 and an Award was passed on 28.08.1985, fixing compensation at 92,258/- of which only 53,375/- was paid to Siddappa.

2(c). The plaintiff submits that the acquisition was quashed by the Hon'ble Karnataka High Court in W.P.No.2945/1983 by its Order dated 02.03.1984 and upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Munivenkatamma vs Gok Principal Secretary on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18503609/

26. Issue No.2: - The plaintiff argues that the sale deeds executed by defendant No.3 to defendant No.4 on 21.06.1990 and by defendant No.4 to defendant No.5 on 29.08.2003 are void, as the acquisition was quashed, leaving defendant No.3 without title.

She relies on "Narayana Reddy" (ILR 1991 KAR 2248) and "HMT Society" (ILR 1995(3) KAR 1962), claiming these judgments nullified the acquisition of Survey No.66/5.
27.
The defendant No.5 counters that the 1981 Notification in LAQ (1) SR 12/1981-82 was never quashed.
The "Narayana Reddy" and "HMT Society" cases dealt with different Notifications of the year 1986/1988, as confirmed by the Hon'ble Karnataka High Court in W.A.No.446/2020.
Siddappa's own challenge to the 1981 Notification in W.P.No.3841/1995 was dismissed on 08.07.1998 for delay and latches and no appeal was filed, rendering the acquisition final.

28. The plaintiff's reliance on W.A.No.6017-18/1997, which declared sale deeds by Rangadama Shetty void, is misplaced, as it pertains to the second phase of acquisition in Dommalur, not the 1981 Notification.
The sale deeds of defendant No.5 are supported by possession certificate, BDA khatha and sanctioned construction, indicating a prima facie valid title.
29. The plaintiff's claim that defendant No.3's layout lacked BDA approval is contradicted by defendant No.5's evidence of sanctioned plan license No.90/03-04.
The dismissal of W.P.No.30139/1999 on 29.07.2004 relates to modifications, not the original layout approval.
The COD enquiry at Ex.P.17 and FIR at Ex.P.18 addresses mismanagement by defendant No.3's Office Bearers, not the validity of allottees' titles.
30. The plaintiff's settlement deed at Ex.P.41 is unregistered and lacks corroboration, raising doubts about her title.
The quashing of the restoration order in W.A.No.446/2020 further undermines her claim that defendant No.3 lacked title to execute the sale deeds.
The plaintiff has failed to prove that the sale deeds dated 21.06.1990 and 29.08.2003 are not binding on her.
Hence, Issue No. 2 is answered in the negative.
31. Issue No.3:-
The plaintiff alleges that defendant No.5's multi-storied building on suit schedule-B property is illegal, as it was constructed without valid title, post-quashing of the acquisition.
She seeks mandatory injunction for its demolition.
32. The defendant No.5 has obtained sanctioned building plan license No.90/03-04 and bank loan for construction in 2003-04, indicating compliance with legal requirements.
The building has been used as serviced apartments since 2003, with tax payments and utility bills as per Ex.D.1 to D.3 confirming continuous possession.
33. The plaintiff's claim hinges on the acquisition being quashed, which, as discussed, is not applicable to the 1981 Notification.

The Hon'ble High Court's ruling in W.A.No.446/2020 confirms Munivenkatamma vs Gok Principal Secretary on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18503609/
10 the validity of acquisition, supporting defendant No.5's title and construction.
The plaintiff's admission that defendant No.5 is in possession of suit schedule-B property further weakens her claim of illegality.
The plaintiff has failed to prove that defendant No.5's construction is illegal.
Hence, Issue No.3 is answered in the negative.
34. Issue No.4:- The plaintiff alleges harassment and interference by defendant Nos.3 to 5, citing their money, muscle power and political influence.

She invokes the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 1989, supported by the Letter of Deputy Commissioner at Ex.P.46, dated 07.01.2011.
35.
The defendant No.5 denies these allegations, labeling them defamatory and reserving the right to initiate action.
The Deputy Commissioner's protection order was stayed on 18.06.2012 in RRT (N) CR/56/09-10 and the plaintiff has not produced specific evidence of interference or threats beyond general assertions.
36. Given defendant No.5's established possession and the plaintiff's failure to prove her own possession, the claim of interference lacks substantiation.
The plaintiff's status as a Scheduled Caste widow does not automatically entitle her to relief without evidence of actionable wrongs under the SC/ST Act.
The plaintiff has failed to prove interference by defendant Nos.3 to 5.
Hence, Issue No.4 is answered in the negative.

37. Issue No.5:- The plaintiff's claims for declaration, permanent injunction, mandatory injunction and encumbrance entry depend on proving her title, possession and the invalidity of defendants'
sale deeds.
As discussed, she has failed to establish these prerequisites.

38. The dismissal of similar suit in O.S.No.4626/2012 on 31.10.2023, where the court held that the 1981 Notification was not quashed and the plaintiff's reliance on "Narayana Reddy"
and "HMT Society" was misplaced, is persuasive.
The principles of constructive res judicata apply, as Siddappa's challenge to the acquisition in W.P.No.3841/1995 was dismissed, binding the plaintiff as his successor.
39. The suit is also procedurally defective, as injunction cannot be granted without a declaratory relief on title as held in Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (AIR 2008 SC 2033).

The defendant No.5 has relied on the following case laws in support of his case;
opennyai_summary.facts:
The plaintiff has filed this suit seeking the following reliefs:
(a) Declaration that the sale deed dated 21.06.1990 executed by defendant No.3 in favour of defendant No.4 and sale deed dated 29.08.2003 executed by defendant No.4 in favour of defendant No.5 are not binding on the plaintiff in respect of suit schedule-B property.
2(b). In 1981, the State of Karnataka - defendant No.1 issued a Notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act bearing No.LAQ (1) SR 12/1981-82, dated 28.12.1981 to acquire 82 acres 19 guntas, including Survey No.66/5, for the benefit of Amarajyothi House Building Co-operative Society - defendant No.3.
HMT House Building Co- operative Society v. Syed Khadar (ILR 1995(3) KAR 1962).
The Hon'ble Supreme Court directed restoration of the land to original owners upon refund of compensation.
2(g). The defendant No.5 constructed a multi-storied building on suit schedule-B property, which the plaintiff claims is illegal due to lack of title.
She seeks the relief of mandatory injunction for its demolition.
The plaintiff approached the Government to enforce the restoration order of Hon'ble Supreme Court, leading to directives from the Special Deputy Commissioner and BBMP to register the khatha in her name.
She paid development charges.
Despite a notice issued to defendant No.3 on 31.03.2012, under Section 125 of the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, no action was taken.
The plaintiff has sought to declare the sale deed executed by defendant No.3 in favour of defendant No.4 and sale deed executed by defendant No.4 in favour of defendant No.5 as non-binding on the plaintiff.
Further, the plaintiff has sought permanent injunction restraining defendant Nos.3 to 5 from interfering with the plaintiff's possession of suit schedule-A property.
Further, the plaintiff has sought mandatory injunction to demolish the structure on suit schedule-B property and direction to the Sub-Registrar - defendant No.6 to enter encumbrances in official records.
4(e). The plaintiff's katha registration with BBMP is claimed to be fraudulent, obtained without inspection and in violation of Section 114A of the Karnataka Municipal Corporation Act.
The defendant No.5 secured status-quo orders from the Deputy Commissioner on 18.06.2012 in RRT (N) CR/56/09-10 and the Joint Commissioner, BBMP.
4(f).
The suit is deemed not maintainable, as the plaintiff seeks an injunction without first establishing title through the declaratory relief.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court directed restoration of the land to owners upon refund of compensation Ex.P.50.
12.
The plaintiff's restoration orders were quashed in W.A.No.446/2020 and her SLP is pending.
The plaintiff admitted in cross-examination on 05.04.2019 that defendant No.5 is in possession of suit schedule-B property, contradicting her claim of peaceful possession.
The plaintiff has failed to prove peaceful possession and enjoyment of suit schedule-B property.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the plaintiff proves that she is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule 'B' property?
2. Whether the plaintiff proves that the alleged registered Sale Deed dated 21.06.1990 executed by the 3rd defendant in favour of 4th defendant and registered Sale Deed dated 29.08.2003 executed by the 4th defendant in favour of 5th defendant in respect of the suit schedule 'B' property is not binding on her?
3. Whether the plaintiff further proves that the 5th defendant has illegally constructed the building over the suit schedule 'B' property as alleged?
4. Whether the plaintiff proves alleged interference by the defendants No.3 to 5?
5. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the reliefs sought for?
6. What order or decree?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
She relies on "Narayana Reddy" (ILR 1991 KAR 2248) and "HMT Society" (ILR 1995(3) KAR 1962), claiming these judgments nullified the acquisition of Survey No.66/5.
27.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The plaintiff has failed to prove that the sale deeds dated 21.06.1990 and 29.08.2003 are not binding on her.
She seeks mandatory injunction for its demolition.
The Deputy Commissioner's protection order was stayed on 18.06.2012 in RRT (N) CR/56/09-10 and the plaintiff has not produced specific evidence of interference or threats beyond general assertions.
36. Given defendant No.5's established possession and the plaintiff's failure to prove her own possession, the claim of interference lacks substantiation.
The plaintiff's status as a Scheduled Caste widow does not automatically entitle her to relief without evidence of actionable wrongs under the SC/ST Act.
The plaintiff has failed to prove interference by defendant Nos.3 to 5.
37. Issue No.5:- The plaintiff's claims for declaration, permanent injunction, mandatory injunction and encumbrance entry depend on proving her title, possession and the invalidity of defendants'
sale deeds.
The principles of constructive res judicata apply, as Siddappa's challenge to the acquisition in W.P.No.3841/1995 was dismissed, binding the plaintiff as his successor.

40. Issue No.6: - In view of the findings on Issue Nos.1 to 5, the plaintiff's suit is liable to be dismissed.

Hence, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is hereby dismissed.
